title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 187
paragraphs: So it is with these matters. But in the region west of Lake Tritonis the Libyans are no longer nomads, and they do not practice the same customs, nor do they do to their children anything like what the nomads do. For the nomad Libyans—whether all of them I cannot say for certain, but many of them—do the following. When their children are four years old, they burn with a greasy piece of sheep's wool the veins in the crowns of their heads, and some of them burn the veins of the temples, so that for the rest of their lives the cold humor may not run down from their heads and harm them. For this reason, they say, they are so healthy; for the Libyans are in truth the healthiest of all peoples we know of—whether for this reason or not I cannot say for certain, but the healthiest they certainly are. If, when they burn the children, a convulsion comes on, they have found a remedy: they pour the urine of a he-goat on them, and so save them. I report what the Libyans themselves report.
